dimensions.label: Reach
dimensions.question: Can the setup act safely at the required distance?

dimensions.label: Recovery
dimensions.question: How safely can the character defend or move after committing?

dimensions.label: Resource pressure
dimensions.question: Does the setup preserve stamina, Spirit, ammunition or consumables?

dimensions.label: Control
dimensions.question: Can it interrupt, reposition or contain the target group?

dimensions.label: Mobility
dimensions.question: Can it enter, exit and reposition without losing control?

dimensions.label: Defensive safety
dimensions.question: How reliably does it survive missed reads and crowded terrain?

dimensions.label: Terrain tolerance
dimensions.question: Does it remain usable on slopes, ledges, interiors and uneven ground?

archetypes.title: Field-Balanced
archetypes.objective: Maintain a dependable mix of defence, movement, reach and resource control during general exploration.
tradeoffs: Does not maximise a single pressure tool.
Must be re-tested when the terrain or target count changes.
protocol: Use the same open-world route three times.
Record healing, stamina/Spirit pressure and forced disengagements.
Change only one weapon or skill choice between trials.

archetypes.title: Defensive Control
archetypes.objective: Prioritise safe reads, guard or shield utility, target containment and low-risk recovery.
tradeoffs: Can reduce mobility or ranged coverage.
Shield-specific behaviour is currently affected by Damiane's Shield Toss death-state issue.
protocol: Test against the same aggressive target without changing difficulty or arena.
Record failed guards, emergency healing and unsafe recovery windows.
Repeat after a save/reload when testing Damiane shield behaviour.

archetypes.title: Aerial Mobility
archetypes.objective: Use confirmed character movement tools to preserve positioning and terrain access.
tradeoffs: Aerial movement does not itself prove higher damage or safety.
Inputs and useful follow-ups differ by character and patch history.
protocol: Choose one terrain route with elevation changes.
Record failed transitions, unsafe landings and actions available immediately after movement.
Repeat without the aerial tool to identify the actual utility gained.

archetypes.title: Ranged Pressure
archetypes.objective: Create distance, maintain target access and test ammunition or reload pressure without assuming a universal damage advantage.
tradeoffs: Ammunition, reload and target-selection behaviour can dominate results.
Close terrain or small targets may invalidate an otherwise stable test.
protocol: Fix target, range and ammunition before each trial.
Record missed targeting, reload interruptions and forced melee transitions.
Re-test while sliding only after a stationary baseline exists.

archetypes.title: Heavy Impact
archetypes.objective: Test commitment-heavy attacks, crowd displacement and large-target pressure under controlled recovery conditions.
tradeoffs: Long commitments can create unsafe recovery windows.
Heavy-object and weapon behaviour changed across patches, so old performance clips are not canonical evidence.
protocol: Use one repeatable group or large target.
Record interruptions, recovery punishment and resource depletion rather than only successful hits.
Do not compare damage unless equipment, target state and inputs are held constant.

archetypes.title: Unarmed Chain
archetypes.objective: Evaluate bare-hand chains, kicks and finishers for control, recovery and weapon-independent reliability.
tradeoffs: Confirmed skill availability does not establish equal character performance.
Range and crowd exposure must be tested separately from combo completion.
protocol: Test a fixed short chain before adding finishers.
Record dropped inputs, target displacement and post-chain safety.
Compare against the same character's weapon baseline rather than another character.

archetypes.title: Boss Reliability
archetypes.objective: Prefer repeatable defence, camera control, healing access and consistent punish windows over peak unverified output.
tradeoffs: A conservative setup may extend the encounter.
Boss arena, camera and phase behaviour can invalidate cross-boss comparisons.
protocol: Use the same boss or Memory Fragment rematch for at least three trials.
Record deaths, healing use, missed punish windows and camera failures.
Change one loadout element only after a repeatable baseline is established.

archetypes.title: Exploration Utility
archetypes.objective: Balance traversal, interaction access, safe combat and low interruption cost during long world routes.
tradeoffs: Story or faction progression may still require Kliff.
Traversal access and combat efficiency should be measured separately.
protocol: Use a route containing travel, gathering and one combat interruption.
Record character-switch requirements, traversal failures and inventory/resource stops.
Do not score route speed until path and interaction order are identical.
